accept.why: As One's (owner, q153: match One): a word to peek at is the word's own width and 36 pt tall, with One's 4-pt hit slop (apps/heartseed/src/sayit/draw.tsx, Peek)

As One's at the largest text: Listen sits in One's fixed round button (apps/heartseed/src/sayit/draw.tsx, BigButton: 132 pt round, its label 17 pt semibold growing with Dynamic Type), whose reference at accessibility-extra-extra-extra-large cuts the word at the circle's edge; the port lets it run 6 px past the edge. Listed for the owner (hs-largest round 1, One has it too)

As One's on iOS at the largest text: Appearance's three choices share one row of equal cells that never wraps (apps/heartseed/src/appearance/choice.tsx: group row, radio flex 1), so the words cannot all fit; the port's last choice runs 2 pt past the side (hs-largest round 1)

As One's on iOS at the largest text: a list's heading, caption, Practice and its line sit above the scroll (apps/heartseed/src/list/screen.tsx, top over ScrollView), and One's reference list.page at accessibility-extra-extra-extra-large cuts that header at the screen's foot with no verse shown; the port shows Practice (its foot under the tab bar) and cuts the line by 54 pt. Listed for the owner (hs-largest round 1, One has it too)

The web's measure, not a spill: the licences keep their spaces as One's text does (white-space pre-wrap), and Chrome's text range counts the space that hangs past a wrapped line's end; with the spaces collapsed (pre-line) the same check finds nothing, and verify ios finds no licence at the largest text (hs-largest round 1)
